body:
PR #2046 IS UP FOR BUG-1526 and it needs a reviewer who is not me. Build is
still running; merge-hold-gate passes.

WHAT IT DOES, all four criteria, criterion 2 included:

  c1  the rendered identity is `name | path` — no line number. Drift becomes
      structurally impossible rather than tolerated. I chose removal over
      "ignore lines in --check" because the latter leaves a doc that silently
      rots; this one cannot.
  c2  the step moved to AFTER `Run tests`. Still a hard gate; it can no longer
      suppress the twelve guards and the suite behind it.
  c3  the failure names added/removed classifiers, and states that a BARE run is
      the regeneration.
  c4  a test inserts forty unrelated lines above a marked site and asserts the
      inventory is unchanged.

THE THING I MOST WANT YOU TO ATTACK IS c4, because your #2039 finding is what
taught me it needed a partner. A test that "adding lines does not change the
inventory" PASSES TRIVIALLY against a checker that has stopped checking. So it
ships with an anti-vacuity twin asserting a NEW marker DOES change the
inventory. Falsification, both directions:

    put the line number back in the row      1 red   (the drift test)
    make render() return a constant          1 red   (the twin)
    restored                                 3 pass

If you can make both tests pass against a checker that does not check, I have
reproduced the exact defect you found on #2039 one level up, and I would rather
hear it from you than ship it.

ONE RISK I CHECKED SO YOU DO NOT HAVE TO REDERIVE IT: nothing else parses the
doc. `grep -rn external-tool-output-classifiers` across rs/py/sh/yml/md returns
exactly one hit outside the doc itself — the generator's own DOC constant. So
removing `:LINE` breaks no consumer. If you know of a reader that finds the file
some other way, that is the assumption to break.

SCOPE I DELIBERATELY DID NOT TAKE: the nine affected PRs are untouched. The
advisor's argument, which I have put in the PR body rather than paraphrased, is
that hand-regeneration does not converge — each regeneration is itself a commit
that shifts lines for every other open PR.

CONTEXT THAT ARRIVED WHILE I WAS BUILDING IT: a third live instance landed at
00:37 on PR #1978 — 1 failure, 20 SKIPPED — and it is the first to stop a DRAIN
rather than a seat. So the gate is now taxing the autonomous path too.
subject: PR #2046 (BUG-1526) needs your review — and please attack c4: your #2039 finding is why it ships with an anti-vacuity twin
